title: Twin gyrostabilizer for a USV
imageAlt: Gyrostabilizer project hardware on an unmanned surface vehicle in a test pool
imageNote: Original gyrostabilizer project photo supplied by Affan Iman, showing the hardware and pool-test setup.
purpose: Develop and test a twin gyrostabilizer to reduce roll motion in an unmanned surface vehicle. This was my Mechatronics Engineering final-year project at Universiti Sains Malaysia, within a USM / PETRONAS Research project.
contribution: Designed and tested a twin-flywheel system using BLDC motors, servo actuation, PID control, and IMU-based state estimation. Integrated the hardware and control elements, then evaluated the system through bench and pool testing.
decisions: Mechanical and electrical integration of the flywheels, motors, and actuators.
IMU feedback and PID control for stabilization.
Experimental comparison of roll response and settling time.
verification: Under the tested conditions, maximum roll reduced from approximately 35° to 10°, and settling time from 15.85 s to 4.10 s. These figures are reported in my resume; original test plots are not yet displayed here.

title: IoT Integrated Smart Plantation System
imageAlt: Slideshow of the Mechatron Masters project poster, team with the prototype, and team with advisor Prof Rizal
imageNote: Original project poster and team photographs supplied by Affan Iman, presented as a photo slideshow.
purpose: Develop a connected greenhouse prototype that combines plant monitoring and actuation with an IoT interface. Presented by the USM Mechatron Masters team for Smart Uni IoT Hackathon National Edition 2023.
contribution: The team integrated Arduino and ESP32 controllers, ESP32-CAM, environmental sensors, pumps, motor drivers and servos with Arduino IoT Cloud and Blynk 2.0. My individual role will be detailed in the case study.
decisions: Soil monitoring and irrigation, with moisture, temperature and humidity readings.
Rain alert and motorised sunroof, dual-axis solar tracking and rainwater harvesting.
verification: Original team and prototype photographs, a photograph with advisor Prof Rizal, and the team project report. No quantitative performance claims are added.

title: Neuroflex — IoT Smart Glove
subtitle: Finger movements translated into caregiver messages.
imageAlt: Neuroflex glove prototype with DIY finger sensors, connecting wires and breadboard electronics on a workbench
imageNote: Original Neuroflex project photograph supplied by Affan Iman. The assembled glove and breadboard electronics are shown without altering the prototype.
purpose: Develop an IoT smart-glove prototype to help people with limited mobility communicate with a caregiver using finger movements. Different finger movements are mapped to predefined messages and sent to a caregiver's device through an IoT connection.
contribution: Worked on an 8051 microcontroller mini project programmed in Assembly using Keil C51. The team built a wearable glove with DIY flex sensors, integrated the electronics and developed the finger-movement-to-message workflow. Learning the low-level code required research, debugging and repeated hardware testing.
decisions: Map different finger movements to distinct caregiver messages.
Develop and debug the 8051 firmware in Assembly using Keil C51.
Build DIY flex sensors as a lower-cost alternative to commercial sensors.
Integrate the wearable electronics and IoT communication workflow.
verification: Original photographs show the assembled prototype and a wearable bench demonstration. This is an undergraduate proof of concept; no clinical validation or patient-trial results are claimed.

extraMedia.caption: Wearable demonstration of the Neuroflex glove, showing finger sensors and the connected prototype electronics.
